own_solution.law: Poiseuille flow gives Q = πr^4ρgh/(8ηL). Combining this with A dh/dt = -Q and integrating gives t = [8ηLA/(πρgr^4)] ln(h_initial/h_final). The time constant is 2138.64 s; divide the resulting time by 60 for minutes.
assumptions: Use the explicitly stipulated steady laminar flow model with hydrostatic driving pressure and negligible end effects and outflow kinetic energy.
The tank has constant cross-sectional area, and the oil has constant density and viscosity.
Oil in the separate bucket does not enter the tank.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: T75EB and T7A3F replace 13 cm with an unspecified increase, violating the review instructions' requirement that sentence variants preserve the numerical quantity and unit, despite being deliberately designated numeral-free controls.

counterexamples: An increase of 1 cm satisfies 'a little deeper' but does not preserve the 13 cm increase specified in the corresponding numbered sentence.
notes: The physical classifications, wiring, governing relations and all certified answers are correct. For relevant additions of 7, 13 and 21 cm, the times are respectively 22.5011, 26.7835 and 31.7944 min. Every disconnected addition leaves the time at 16.7528 min. The explicitly claimed minimal pairs T7B4A/T3C55 and TFF4D/TD265 preserve the number and unit. Pass 2 explains that the two other controls intentionally omit them; this explains their construction but does not provide an exception to the frozen review requirement. The pass-1 verdict therefore remains unchanged. Its answers were expressed in seconds; they agree with the authors' minute values after conversion. SI inputs make the displayed time relations yield seconds.
